arxiv-2205-01792.title: Growth of groups with linear Schreier graphs
arxiv-2205-01792.creator: Laurent Bartholdi, Volodymyr Nekrashevych, Tianyi Zheng
arxiv-2205-01792.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Laurent Bartholdi, Volodymyr Nekrashevych, Tianyi Zheng. Introduction We introduce here a new method of proving upper estimates of growth of finitely generated groups and constructing groups of intermediate growth using graphs of their actions.

arxiv-2210-10165.title: Episodic accretion and mergers during growth of massive protostars 2022 Episodic accretion and mergers during growth of massive protostars – A
arxiv-2210-10165.creator: Vardan G. Elbakyan, Sergei Nayakshin, Dominique M.-A. Meyer, Eduard I. Vorobyov
arxiv-2210-10165.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Vardan G. Elbakyan, Sergei Nayakshin, Dominique M.-A. Meyer, Eduard I. Vorobyov. 3D simulations of high mass young stellar object (HMYSO) growth show that their circumstellar discs fragment onto multiple self-gravitating objects. Accretion of these by HMYSO may explain episodic accretion bursts discovered recently. We post-process results of a previous 3D simulation of a HMYSO disc with a 1D code that resolves the disc and object dynamics down to the stellar surface.

arxiv-2305-02684.title: Stirling numbers with higher level and records
arxiv-2305-02684.creator: F. A. Shiha
arxiv-2305-02684.description: Abstract In this present paper, we show that the Stirling numbers of the first kind with higher level connected with the probability distribution of the number of records and record times in the so-called F α F^{\alpha} -scheme. In addition, we determine the location of the maximum of the Stirling numbers of the first kind with higher level.

arxiv-2305-11253.title: Dipole Screening in Pure Shear Strain Protocols of Amorphous Solids
arxiv-2305-11253.creator: Chandana Mondal, Michael Moshe, Itamar Procaccia, Saikat Roy
arxiv-2305-11253.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Chandana Mondal, Michael Moshe, Itamar Procaccia, Saikat Roy. When amorphous solids are subjected to simple or pure strain, they exhibit elastic increase in stress, punctuated by plastic events that become denser (in strain) upon increasing the system size. It is customary to assume in theoretical models that the stress released in each plastic event is redistributed according to the linear Eshelby kernel, causing avalanches of additional stress release.

arxiv-2409-07886.title: Non-unital noise in a superconducting quantum computer as a computational resource for reservoir computing
arxiv-2409-07886.creator: Francesco Monzani, Emanuele Ricci, Luca Nigro, Enrico Prati
arxiv-2409-07886.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Francesco Monzani, Emanuele Ricci, Luca Nigro, Enrico Prati. Despite theoretical promises, most machine learning algorithms fail on current quantum computers due to overwhelming noise. Indeed, noise may limit their ability to retain and manipulate information over time, which is especially problematic when dealing with sequential data. Nevertheless, many recurrent architectures are most efficient if they can process information by progressively reducing the correlation on inputs from earlier time steps.

arxiv-2501-15772.title: Random unipotent Sylow subgroups of groups of Lie type of bounded rank
arxiv-2501-15772.creator: Saveliy V. Skresanov
arxiv-2501-15772.description: Abstract In 2001 Liebeck and Pyber showed that a finite simple group of Lie type is a product of 25 25 carefully chosen unipotent Sylow subgroups. Later, in a series of works it was shown that 4 4 unipotent Sylow subgroups suffice.

arxiv-2508-08083.title: Derivation of Dietary Patterns dependent on Diabetes status using ordinal Supervised Robust Profile Clustering: Results from Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos
arxiv-2508-08083.creator: Briana Joy K. Stephenson, Daniela Sotres-Alvarez, Martha Daviglus, Ramon A. Durazo-Arvizu, Yasmin Mossavar-Rahmani, Jianwen Cai
arxiv-2508-08083.description: Abstract The burden of diabetes has disproportionately impacted Hispanic/Latino residents in the United States, with diet recognized as a major modifiable risk factor. Outcome-dependent dietary patterns provide insight into what foods may be associated with the increased severity and progression of diabetes.

arxiv-2510-26343.creator: N. Arancibia Robert

pmc-11340190.creator: Wenqing Wang, Liuting Yu, Zhen Li, Yan Xiao, Hao Jiang, Yan-lai Tang, Yun Chen, Hongman Xue

Given the importance of altered metabolites in the carcinogenesis of pediatric B-ALL, studying the metabolic profile of children with B-ALL during induction chemotherapy and in different minimal residual disease (MRD) status may contribute to the management of pediatric B-ALL.MethodsWe collected paired peripheral blood plasma samples from children with B-ALL at pre- and

pmc-11414253.title: Contraceptive access and use among women with migratory experience living in high-income countries: a scoping review
pmc-11414253.creator: P. Gozzi, M. Persson, A. Nielsen, H. Kilander, A. E. Kågesten, K. Emtell Iwarsson, D. Ljungcrantz, M. Bredell, E. C. Larsson
pmc-11414253.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundWomen who have migrated often encounter difficulties in accessing healthcare and experience inequitable sexual and reproductive health outcomes in destination countries. These health inequities include contraceptive access and use. To better understand what influences contraceptive access and use, this scoping review set out to synthesize the evidence on contraceptive access and use and on associated interventions among women with migratory experience in high-income countries (HICs) in Europe, North America and Australasia.MethodsThe scientific databases PubMed, Web of Science and CINAHL were searched for

pmc-11481822.title: Economic Burden of Community-Acquired Antibiotic-Resistant Urinary Tract Infections: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-11481822.creator: Nina Jiayue Zhu, Misghina Weldegiorgis, Emma Carter, Colin Brown, Alison Holmes, Paul Aylin, Amaryllis Mavragani
pmc-11481822.description: BackgroundAntibiotic resistance (ABR) poses a major burden to global health and economic systems. ABR in community-acquired urinary tract infections (CA-UTIs) has become increasingly prevalent. Accurate estimates of ABR’s clinical and economic burden are needed to support medical resource prioritization and cost-effectiveness evaluations of urinary tract infection (UTI) interventions.

pmc-11622081.title: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy plus common bile duct exploration for extrahepatic bile duct stones and postoperative recurrence-associated risk factors
pmc-11622081.creator: Jia-Hua Liao, Ju-Shi Li, Tie-Long Wang, Wen-Shen Liu
pmc-11622081.description: BACKGROUNDThere remain controversies regarding the surgical treatment of extrahepatic bile duct stones (EHBDSs) in clinical practice.AIMTo explore the curative effect of laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) plus common bile duct exploration (CBDE) for the surgical treatment of EHBDSs and to analyze the risk factors that affect postoperative stone recurrence.METHODSEighty-two patients with EHBDSs admitted between March 2017 and March 2023 were selected.

pmc-12608345.title: Potential Hypotheses Predicting Leaf Litter Nitrogen and Phosphorus Patterns at the Global Scale
pmc-12608345.creator: Yajun Xie, Jiacheng Yan, Yonghong Xie
pmc-12608345.description: Climate has shaped green leaf nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) patterns through its direct physiological effects (Temperature–Plant Physiology hypothesis), indirect pathways involving soil nutrients (Soil Substrate Age hypothesis), or vegetation composition (Species Composition hypothesis). However, the efficiencies of these hypotheses and the relative importance of the factors involved in predicting leaf litter N and P remain unresolved.

pmc-12769619.title: Deacetylasperulosidic Acid Methyl Ester Ameliorates Carbon Tetrachloride-Induced Liver Fibrosis by Suppressing Inflammation and Modulating Gut Microbiota
pmc-12769619.creator: Li Chen, Chunyan Chen, Qixiang Chen, Ting Jiang, Lingli Zheng, Rong Tang, Cheng Wang
pmc-12769619.description: Liver fibrosis is an excessive wound-healing response triggered by chronic liver injury. It may eventually progress to cirrhosis, liver failure or liver cancer. Currently, there are no effective therapeutic strategies available. Deacetylasperulosidic acid methyl ester (DAM), a natural iridoid compound derived from Rubiaceae plants, possesses potential anti-inflammatory activity. However, its role in liver fibrosis and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

pmc-13147209.title: A Self‐Amplifying RNA Lipid Nanoparticle (saRNA‐LNP) Vaccine Provides Effective Protection Against Porcine Epidemic Diarrhea
pmc-13147209.creator: Jinqi Shu, Han Zhang, Fang Wang, Hanyu Zhang, Xin Liu, Keshu Liu, Yinhe Zha, Wenqin Chai, Jianghui Yao, Yujun Lin, Chao Wu, Xiaomin Zhao
pmc-13147209.description: The development of vaccine platforms capable of inducing sustained, potent, and cost‐effective immunity remains a major challenge in veterinary vaccinology, particularly for coronaviruses, which are often associated with short‐lived vaccine‐induced protection. Here, we establish a self‐amplifying RNA (saRNA) lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccine platform and evaluate its application using porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) as a representative coronavirus model.

pmc-13222582.title: Pregnancy Outcomes in Women with Type 1 Diabetes by Socioeconomic and Mental Health Disadvantages

pmc-13222582.description: AimTo examine whether individual-level measures of socioeconomic or mental health disadvantages are associated with preterm delivery and extreme large for gestational age (eLGA) among women with type 1 diabetes.MethodsNationwide register-based study of singleton pregnancies among women with type 1 diabetes, 1997–2021.

pmc-13603204.title: Unravelling the Impact of Diabetes on Insulin-like Growth Factor (IGF) Axis Signalling in Mesenchymal Stem Cells Isolated from the Bone of Knee Joints
pmc-13603204.creator: Nancy Hussein, Josephine L. Meade, Hemant Pandit, Elena Jones, Reem El-Gendy
pmc-13603204.description: Diabetes mellitus (T2DM) represents a major health problem with several potentially life-threatening complications including cardiovascular disease and osteopathy. Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) are a promising candidate for bone regeneration, and the insulin-like growth factor (IGF) axis plays a fundamental role in both bone regeneration and stem cell biology.

pmc-13660966.title: Mapping the Evidence on Vitamin D, Vitamin B12, and Folate Deficiencies and Their Potential Impact on Treatment Outcomes in Patients With Cancer in Sub-Saharan Africa: Protocol for a Scoping Review
pmc-13660966.creator: Olufunmilayo Olukemi Akapo, Olubunmi Margaret Ogbodu, Teke Apalata, Amy Schwartz
pmc-13660966.description: BackgroundMicronutrient deficiencies, particularly of vitamin D, vitamin B12, and folate, are increasingly recognized as important, yet underexplored contributors to adverse outcomes in oncology care. These micronutrients are essential for immune regulation, DNA synthesis and repair, cell proliferation, and metabolic homeostasis, all of which are frequently disrupted in patients with cancer.

uslaw-usc-t28-s2632.title: 28 U.S.C. § 2632 — Commencement of a civil action
uslaw-usc-t28-s2632.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t28-s2632.description: United States Code, Title 28 (Judiciary And Judicial Procedure); Part VI (Particular Proceedings); Chapter 169 (Court Of International Trade Procedure). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Except for civil actions specified in subsections (b) and (c) of this section, a civil action in the Court of International Trade shall be commenced by filing concurrently with the clerk of the court a summons.
